 JUDGMENT The Petitioner filed this petition under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989 claiming compensation from the respondents due to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

Brief facts of Petitioner's case, are as under:
On 03.10.2022 at about 01.45 a.m, (early morning) the Petitioner was traveling in KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, on NH-75 Road, Kolar - Bangalore road,
towards Hoskote, when the bus reached near Mylapura Gate, Hosakote Taluk,
Bangalore Rural District, driver of said bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life at high speed and lost control over the bus and dashed to one Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498, which was parked on left side of the road without any signals or any indication.
As a result of forced impact, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to MVJ Hospital, Hosakote for first aid,
then he was shifted to Jayanagar Orthopaedic Center Bengaluru wherein, he took treatment as inpatient and undergone surgery and spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical expenses,
transportation, conveyance and other charges.
4. It is contended that, this accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus and also due to negligent act of 4 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 the driver of the Lorry.

Hence, Hosakote Police registered a case against driver of the KSRTC bus bearing Ramesh vs K.S.R.T.C on 20 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199618399/
2 Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773 in crime No.353/2022.
5.

It is contended that, prior to the accident the Petitioner was hale, healthy and he was Painter by profession, and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries he is not able to do his job and hence he lost his earning and suffering from mental shock and agony.
6.
In pursuance to the notice, Respondent No.1 to 4 appeared through their respective Counsels and filed written statement separately.

7. Brief averments of the Written statement of Respondent No.1 are as under:
While admitting the ownership of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, this Respondent contended that, this accident occurred not due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC Bus, but due to sole negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498 as he was parked the Lorry without any precautionary measurement and signals.
Hence, Respondent no.2 & 3 are liable to pay the 5 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 compensation to the Petitioners.

However,
on humanitarian ground this Respondent had paid exgratia amount of Rs.11,356/-
and same may be liable to be deducted and in case of holding contributory negligence on the part of the Lorry either fully or partially.
The insurer and owner of the lorry shall be directed to refund the medical expenses paid by this respondent to the Petitioner to the extent of their liability.

8. Brief averments of the Written statement of Respondent No.2 are as under:
The petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case and denied the entire averments of the petition.

While admitting about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498 in favour of Mr.Srinivasa, this Respondent restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that, driver of the said vehicle did not possess valid D.L. FC and permit as on the date of the accident.
hence, terms and conditions of insurance policy were violated.

It is contended that, as per the petition averments this accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the 6 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F- 3773.
9.

Brief averments of the Written statement of Respondent No.3 & 4 are as under:
The petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case and denied the entire averments of the petition.

While admitting the ownership & driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA- 16/D-9498 these Respondents contended that, this accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773.

It is contended that, they took all the safety methods with due Ramesh vs K.S.R.T.C on 20 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199618399/
3 diligence, because of the rash and negligent driving of driver of respondent No.1 this accident was happened.
Respondent No.3 vehicle (Lorry) bearing No.KA-16/D-9498 was breakdown around 1 "o" clock , so lorry driver parked the vehicle left side of the road on the footpath.
He took the safety precautions about the vehicles parking and placed the stones and camphire near the accident place.
The accident occurred due to negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus driver only.
Hence the Respondent no.3 and 4 not liable to pay any compensation to the Petitioner.

Further Respondents denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by him and disability caused to him and also contended that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence , prays to dismiss the petition with costs.

10. On basis of the Pleadings and materials, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, on 03.10.2022 at about 01.45 am, the petitioner was travelling as a commuter in a KSRTC Bus bearing No. KA-57-F-3773 on NH-75 Kolar-Bangalore Road and proceeding towards Hoskote.

when he reached Hoskote Mylapura Gate, at that time all of sudden he raised the speed of the said Bus and lost the control over his vehicle and dashed against Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16-D-9498 parking the vehicle in left of the road without any signal or any indication and without observing the traffic rules.

As a result of forced impact,
petitioner sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. Whether order or award?
In order to substantiate the case, Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got examined two witnesses as Pw.2 and 3.
They got marked 15 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P15.
The Driver of KSRTC bus got examined as RW-1 and not got marked any document on his behalf.

The Manager of 2nd Respondent Insurance company got examined as Rw.2 and got marked two documents as Ex.R1 &
2.
12.
Heard the arguments and Perused the materials available on record.

13. For the following reasons, I answer the above Issues as under:-

REASONS 14. Issue No.1:- The Petitioner filed this petition against Respondents for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.
15.

The Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination and 9 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 in his chief affidavit of examination in chief he had reiterated the averments of petition and got marked 11 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.
16.
Ex.P1 is the Copy of F.I.R., Ex.P2 is the Copy of Complaint.

Ex.P3 is the Copy of Spot sketch,
Ex.P4 is the Copy of spot Mahazar, Ex.P5 is the Copy of IMV report, Ex.P6 is the Copy of Wound certificate, Ex.P7 is the Copy of Charge sheet, Ex.P8 & 9 are the discharge summary, Ex.P10 is the Notarized copy of Aadhaar card and Ex.P11 is the X-rays.
17. Sri
.B.Ramesh the Medical record Officer at Jayanagar, Orthopaedic Center, Bangalore is examined as Pw.2 and got marked two documents as Ex.P12 and 13.
Ex.P12 is the Authorization letter and Ex.P13 is the Inpatient record.
18. Dr.S.A.Somashekar the Orthopaedic Surgeon at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bangalore is examined as Pw.3 and got marked two documents marked as Ex.P14 and 15.
Ex.P14 is the OPD card and Ex.P15 is the X-ray films.
19. Sri.Sharanappa the driver of respondent No.1 KSRTC Bus got examined as Rw.1 and filed 10 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 affidavit in lieu of chief examination.
In his chief affidavit he had reiterated the contents of the Written statement.
In the cross examination he spelt out that, " It is true to suggest that, Police seized our bus.
It is true to suggest that, charge is filed against me.
It is true to suggest that, two passengers husband and wife who were sitting in front seat died at spot.
It is true to suggest that, we are not challenged the spot sketch and mahazar. "
20. Mr.Shreyas Bhat the Manager Legal Claims of the 2nd Respondent / insurance company got examined as Rw.2 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination.
In his chief affidavit he had reiterated the contents of the Written statement.
Further got marked two documents as Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.
Ex.R1 is the Authorization letter and Ex.R2 is the Copy of Insurance policy.
In the cross examination he spelt out that, "It is true to suggest that, lorry was insured with our company and it was valid.

It is true to suggest that, there is no mechanical defect in respect of lorry as per IMV report."
21.

On perusal of Spot sketch and Charge sheet it appears that, near Mylapura Gate Hosakote,
opposite to NH - 75 Hotel, Bangalore driver of 11 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57/F-3773 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner came at high speed and dashed to one Lorry bearing No.KA-16/D-9498 and caused the accident.

The said Lorry which was Ramesh vs K.S.R.T.C on 20 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199618399/
5 parked on the road by its driver without any precautionary measures.
Further IMV report discloses that, the rear portion of the Lorry and front portion of the KSRTC bus were damaged.

Hence,
Hosakote Police filed Charge sheet against driver of the KSRTC Bus as A1 and driver of Lorry as A2.

22 . In the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the claimant has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble APEX Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The so-called reason that as the name of Dheeraj Kumar was not mentioned in the FIR, so it was not possible for Dheeraj Kumar to see the incident, is not a proper assessment of the fact-situation in this case.
It is well known that in a case relating to motor accident claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as it is required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Court must keep this distinction in mind.

Reference in this connection may be made to the decision of this Court in Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, in which the relevant observation on this point has been made and which is very pertinent and is quoted below:-
"In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touch stone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
23. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P1 - F.I.R., Ex.P2 - Complaint.
Ex.P3 - Spot sketch, Ex.P4 - Spot Mahazar, Ex.P5 - IMV report, Ex.P6 - Wound certificate and Ex.P7 Charge sheet

it appears that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773 and also due to negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498.
Accordingly, I answer the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
24. Issue No.2:- The Petitioner claimed the compensation amount of Rs.15,00,000/-.

As per Ex.P3 Wound certificate the Petitioner sustained following injuries:
13 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 1.
Distal 1/3rd both bone fracture of left leg.
2. Parietal region soft tissue injury.

6
The doctor had opined that, above said injuries are grievous in nature.

Hence, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, the Petitioner is entitled for amount of Rs.80,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
25. The Petitioner had not produced even a single medical bill.
However he had produced two discharge summary which are marked as Ex.P8 and 9.
As per Ex,P8 the Petitioner took treatment at Jayanagar Orthopaedic Centre from 03-10-2022 to 08-10-2022.
Ex,P8 discloses that, the Petitioner took treatment at MVJ Hospital from 03-10-2022 to 03-10-2022.

Therefore, by considering the period of treatment taken as inpatient this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.8,000/-
under the head Medical expenses, Transportation, food, Nourishment and conveyance charges.
To prove the assessment of disability, the Petitioner got examined one Doctor Shri.Somashekar as Pw-3.

In the chief examination affidavit the doctor deposed that, on examination it is found that,
the Petitioner walks with pain and limping, Diffuse swelling of left lower limb and Surgical scars are seen over left knee, leg and ankle.
Recent X-ray shows that United fracture of both bones of left leg with implants in situ as both sites.

The doctor assessed the total disability of left lower limb at 42%
and that of to the whole body of the Petitioner at 21%.
In the Cross examination doctor had deposed that, " I am not a treated doctor at any stage.
It is true to suggest that, fractures are united as per recent x-rays.
It is true to suggest that, there is no bone loss and no shortening limb.
It is true to suggest that, as per guidelines 50% of disability of particulars limb cannot taken towards the whole body."
However by considering the nature of the injury and evidence of the doctor, this Tribunal had taken the disability of the Petitioner at 15% to the whole body.

27. It is contended that prior to the accident, the Petitioner was Painter by Profession and was 15 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 earning Rs.25,000/- p.m and due to accidental injuries he is not able to carry on his work as before the accident.
The Petitioner had not produced any document to prove his income and avocation.
In present days the Coolie worker get Rs.500/- to 600/- per day.
However by considering the age and occupation of petitioner this Tribunal taken the monthly income of the Petitioner at Rs.16,000/-.
28. As per Ex.P10 Notarized Copy of Aadhaar card date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 30- 07-1981.
Therefore, age of the Petitioner is taken as 41 years at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier applicable is 14 which comes as follows:
Rs.16,000 x 12 x 14 x 15% = Rs.4,03,200/- Hence, I award Rs.4,03,200/- under the head loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.
29.
Towards future medication the Doctor deposed in his chief examination affidavit that, the Petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants at both sides which would cost around Rs.40,000/-.
In private set up.

Neither the Petitioner nor the doctor had produced estimation for Ramesh vs K.S.R.T.C on 20 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199618399/
7 future 16 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 medication.
However, by considering the nature of injury and evidence of doctor this tribunal awarded Rs.25,000/- under the head future medical expenses.
(which does not carry any interest)
30. The Petitioner was Painter profession and due to accidental injuries his routine work was hampered for some days.

Therefore, by considering this aspect and the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, this tribunal awarded the amount of Rs.15,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities.

31. Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:
 Under the Heads Amount Pain and sufferings Rs. 80,000-00 Medical expenses, Transpor- tation, 8,000-00 food, Nourishment, Conveyance and Rs. attendant charges.
Towards future loss of income on Rs. 4,03,200-00 account of permanent disability Towards future medical expenses Rs. 25,000-00

Towards loss of amenities of life Rs. 15,000-00 Total Rs.
5,31,200-00 17 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,31,200/-.

32. Interest:
For awarding interest

, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest can be awarded in MVC Cases, cannot be more than 6% p.a.

Hence, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
33. Liability:-
The Respondent No.1 is the RC owner-cum- Insurer of KSRTC bus bearing Reg No.KA-57/F- 3773.

Respondent No.2 is the Insurer, Respondent No.3 is the owner and as per the Charge sheet the Respondent No.4 is the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498.
34.
In the Written statement the respondent No.1 KSRTC contended that, they had paid a sum of Rs.11,356/- to the Petitioner on humanitarian ground without admitting the liability.
But the respondent No.1 had not produced any document 18 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 to prove that they had paid the amount of Rs.11,356/- to the Petitioner.
Hence, the said amount cannot be deducted out of total compensation amount.

sentences.text: As already discussed in the issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus driver and also due to negligence in parking of Lorry by it's driver jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

Further, the Respondent No.1 is being RC Owner-cum-Insurer of the KSRTC Bus and Respondent No.2 being Insurer of the Lorry are primarily held liable to pay the 50% each of the compensation amount with interest to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.

36. Issue No.3: for the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act filed by the Petitioners is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,31,200/- (Rupees five lakh, thirty one thousand and two hundred only) with interest @ 6% p.a., (excluding future medical expenses) from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay aforesaid compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Petition against Respondent No.4 (i.e., driver of offending vehicle) is hereby dismissed.

Out of total compensation amount, the Respondent No.1 is being owner of KSRTC bus and the Respondent No.2 being Insurer of the Lorry are directed to deposit 50% each together with 6%
interest p.a. within 60 days, from the date of this Order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner after proper verification and identification of documents.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
20 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022
Draw the award accordingly.

In the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the claimant has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble APEX Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others.
The so-called reason that as the name of Dheeraj Kumar was not mentioned in the FIR, so it was not possible for Dheeraj Kumar to see the incident, is not a proper assessment of the fact-situation in this case.
It is well known that in a case relating to motor accident claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as it is required to be done in a criminal trial.
Reference in this connection may be made to the decision of this Court in Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, in which the relevant observation on this point has been made and which is very pertinent and is quoted below:-
"In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest can be awarded in MVC Cases, cannot be more than 6% p.a.
In the Written statement the respondent No.1 KSRTC contended that, they had paid a sum of Rs.11,356/- to the Petitioner on humanitarian ground without admitting the liability.
But the respondent No.1 had not produced any document 18 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 to prove that they had paid the amount of Rs.11,356/- to the Petitioner.
Hence, the said amount cannot be deducted out of total compensation amount.
As already discussed in the issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus driver and also due to negligence in parking of Lorry by it's driver jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
